html:
A faith that grew out of Ismaili Islam in Fatimid Cairo in 1017, around the teaching that the caliph al-Hakim was a manifestation of the one God. Its followers call themselves the people of unity, and its strongholds are the mountains of Lebanon, Syria and northern Israel.

Its first preachers were Hamza ibn Ali and al-Darazi, from whom outsiders took the name Druze, though the Druze reject him. After al-Hakim vanished in 1021 the movement was persecuted in Egypt and moved to the hills of the Levant. In 1043 the call to new members was closed. Since then no one has been able to convert in, and Druze marry only Druze.

They believe in one God and in the rebirth of souls. Their scriptures, the Epistles of Wisdom, are read only by initiates, and many teachings are kept private. They draw on Islam and on Greek thought, including Neoplatonism. Druze emirs such as Fakhr al-Din II ruled Mount Lebanon under the Ottomans, and Druze communities still play a large role in the politics of Lebanon.
